clue.text: Message from sovereign on currency

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A royal communication is printed on a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in an across clue the sovereign simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage the word meant a message carried for someone, before it came to mean a trip made to deliver one.

clue.text: Limit intended for French novel with everything

parts.note: roman is French for novel
all means everything

explanation.surface: A boundary meant to apply to a French novel and everything in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hadrian's Wall in northern England was built as the Roman empire's limit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans built their wall across Britain to mark the frontier of the empire.

clue.text: Certify being at match

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for having been present at the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness that something is true, to certify it.

clue.text: Mother nested wrongly having done her best

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: wrongly arranged letters are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A mother bird has built her nest badly despite trying hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' is DAM, the word for an animal's mother, not a human parent; 'wrongly' scrambles the word nested.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's damnedest is an idiom for doing one's utmost, one's best.

clue.text: Letters go to the French and bingo!

parts.note: Litt. is the abbreviation for letters, as in the degree D.Litt.
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone sends off letters to France and shouts bingo in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bingo' lacks its capital: it is Bingo Little, the hapless friend of Bertie Wooster in P.G. Wodehouse's comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is the first name of the Wodehouse character whose surname this is.

clue.text: Broadly inadequate as foil to 5 across

indicators.note: inadequate is read as falling short, the E at the end giving way to a zero, O

parts.note: large is the opposite of 5 across, as in the comedy duo Little and Large

explanation.surface: Something too small as a contrast to its partner, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Little and Large were a British TV comedy double act. The setter's own solution swaps LARGE's E for O; it is a loose device.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction meaning slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Destiny travelled east from northeast

indicators.note: letters that have travelled have moved about into new positions

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Fate journeyed eastwards from the northeast of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelled' scrambles the letters of destiny. Tyneside is the Newcastle area of northeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyneside, round Newcastle, is a region of northeast England.

clue.text: All that's unusual in a girl's name

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement puts the letters in a different order

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Everything that is odd about a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leila is a female first name, of Arabic origin.

clue.text: Indication of extended writing about my return with cat

indicators.note: return turns the whole of that combination back to front
the postscript wraps around the word 'my', one piece outside the other

parts.note: a PS, postscript, extends a letter already written
taken as written
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A sign of having written at length about my homecoming with the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the word my inside the postscript abbreviation, and 'return' turns that whole unit back to front before the cat is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or indication of an underlying condition, especially of illness.

clue.text: Where someone lives, say, with lighter garment

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a person's dwelling is some address

explanation.surface: A person's home, so to speak, comes with lighter clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn in warm weather is lighter than winter wear; a frock for hot days is an example.

clue.text: Management of sport in contest?

definitions.meaning: a race is a contest in which the sport is going on foot at speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both operating an enterprise and the athletic pursuit of racing on foot.

clue.text: Fruit, not good and bad, in the business of saving the planet?

definitions.text: the business of saving the planet?

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for good is left out of the fruit

parts.note: a greengage is a kind of plum

indicators.note: bad letters are spoiled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plum, spoiled and rotten, in an environmental enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: GREENGAGE without a G gives GREENAGE; 'bad' turns AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Policies to protect the environment make up a programme of environmentalism.

clue.text: Public servant drunk Foster's in small gallery

indicators.note: the jumbled beer name sits inside the pair of words for small and gallery

parts.note: mini means small
the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: a drunk beer is a mixed-up one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Australian lager name, its S included

explanation.surface: A civil servant downs a lager in a tiny art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the lager's name, and 'in' places the scramble between the words for small and gallery. Foster's is an Australian beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior government minister is a holder of public office, serving the public.

clue.text: Antelope with no end vigorous style

indicators.note: with no end tells us the antelope's final letter is dropped

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope's bounding gait admired for its vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash or flair, a lively and confident manner.

clue.text: Needed support of the "ass of the bridge" unfinished in France

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
ane (âne) is French for ass

indicators.note: unfinished cuts the last letter from the French phrase

parts.note: du pont is French for 'of the bridge'

explanation.surface: Someone relied on a famous saying about the donkey and the bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells us to translate the quoted phrase into French: le âne du pont, with the final T of PONT dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean upon someone is to rely on them, needing their support.

clue.text: Fed and fed, eating original first

indicators.note: the word for fed swallows the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: noshed means ate, fed oneself
ur- is a prefix meaning original
I is the Roman numeral for one, first

explanation.surface: A creature fed twice, eating the first thing it found.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed, so nourished means given food.

clue.text: Right to take one sixth part of course in physical education

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the abbreviation for school sport

parts.note: PE is the school abbreviation for physical education
R, from Latin recipe, means take, seen on prescriptions
I is the Roman numeral one
VI is the Roman numeral six
a leg is a stage of a course or journey

explanation.surface: A claim to take a sixth of the course in a games lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or entitlement.

clue.text: Sandglass, say, with tiger worried about start of meal

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say

indicators.note: the jumbled cat goes round the letter from the meal
a worried animal is agitated, so its letters are thrown about
start of selects the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An hourglass, for instance, with a tiger fretting before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges TIGER to TIER, which 'about' wraps round M.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-filled timer is used to time boiling eggs.

clue.text: Fight duel stupidly with student that's very nice

indicators.note: a stupidly fought fight is a disorderly one, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A foolish duel fought by a student, which is said to be lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges FIGHTDUEL to DELIGHTFU before L.
explanation.definitionFit: Delightful means highly pleasing, a stronger word for very nice.

clue.text: Gilbertian with 17 26 and great 15s, chiefly 9 on 5 across 1s for his 11s

definitions.text: Gilbertian with 17 26 and great 15s, chiefly 9 on 5 across 1s for his 11s

parts.words: Gilbertian with 17 26 and great 15s, chiefly 9 on 5 across 1s for his 11s
parts.note: with the cross-references filled in this quotes the song in The Gondoliers by Gilbert and Sullivan describing the ruler of Barataria, whose duties are delightful and privileges great

explanation.walkthrough: The Gondoliers song 'Rising early in the morning' says the duties are delightful and the privileges great, and the ruler runs little errands for the ministers of state.
explanation.definitionFit: The two gondoliers in the opera jointly reign as monarch of Barataria, and the song lists that ruler's tasks.

clue.text: Much of 11 on two Scots rivers points to set of tunnels

parts.note: most of 11 across is the word minister, and a rabbi is a Jewish minister
twa is Scots for two
R is the abbreviation for river, twice
E and N are compass points

explanation.surface: Part of a government role sits upon two Scottish rivers that point to burrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of 11' takes MINISTER from MINISTER OF STATE; a rabbi is a minister of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A connected system of burrows dug by rabbits is a network of tunnels.

clue.text: Vote 1 — if on car it applied, example of 10?

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone in

indicators.note: letters applied in a new way are rearranged into a different order

parts.note: the figure 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Vote for the first one, if on the car it was put to use as an example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' rearranges I plus IFONCARIT to RIFICATION. The 10 is GREEN AGENDA: electrifying cars is a green policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting transport to electric power is a typical policy of environmental campaigners.

clue.text: Musical note on sequel to 12 left out

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: left out drops L, the abbreviation for left

parts.note: élan vital is a phrase, so vital is what follows 12 across

explanation.surface: A musical note added to a follow-up that has been omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Élan vital is Bergson's term for the life force; VITAL without L gives VITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Ran a mile from Khan?

parts.note: a means one, the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fled a long way from a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Imran Khan was a Pakistani cricket captain and later prime minister; 'Khan?' defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Imran is the first name of the cricketer and politician whose surname is the defining word.

clue.text: Gleam unevenly — keep boiling when drunk?

indicators.note: when drunk the word is slurred, an S turning to SH in a tipsy voice

parts.note: to simmer is to keep something just at the boil

explanation.surface: Something glints irregularly, as if the pot kept bubbling after too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMMER said by someone drunk comes out with a slur as SHIMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmer is to shine with a wavering, flickering light.

clue.text: Painter on top of stove to pour out the tea?

parts.note: the hob is the top of a cooker
the person who pours tea is said to be mother, so 'be ma' means pour

explanation.surface: An artist sits on top of the cooker to serve the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain whoever pours the tea is asked 'shall I be mother?', so 'be ma' is pouring. Meindert Hobbema was a Dutch landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Meindert Hobbema was a seventeenth-century Dutch landscape artist.

clue.text: See 19
Jobs of the French with restrictions

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
ties are bonds that restrict

explanation.surface: French employment comes with strings attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties are tasks one is required to perform, as jobs are.
